final_message:
I couldn't reproduce the bug, so I haven't changed anything.

In `src/slugify.py`, `slugify('Hello,  World!')` returns `'hello-world'`, which is the output you wanted. The 5 existing tests pass. The function lowercases the text and collapses each run of non-alphanumeric characters into a single `-`. It then strips leading and trailing dashes, so the `,  ` becomes one dash and the trailing `!` leaves nothing behind.

The output users report, `'hello---world-'`, looks like what you'd get from an older version without the `+` in the regex and without the `.strip("-")`. So they may be running a stale install or a different copy of the code. It may be worth checking which version they have.

If you can point me to where they're seeing it, such as another module, a vendored copy or a different branch, I'll look there. This directory isn't a git repo, so I can't check the history myself.
